deviations.what: Two of the pre-existing tests in tests/test_permissions.py were edited: test_a_permission_granted_directly_to_the_person_answers_the_same_way (rewritten to assert refusal, renamed test_a_permission_granted_directly_to_the_person_is_refused) and test_a_model_level_permission_held_through_a_group_answers_for_any_instance (its arbitrary 'Some Role' group changed to an actual shipped role, PortalRoles.DATA_CURATOR.name). Neither is one of the four tests named in D20 or protected by this brief's prohibitions.
deviations.why: These two tests encoded T011's original, wider acceptance (a direct grant, or membership of any group, answers the same way as a role) - the exact reading this fix narrows. Leaving them asserting the old behaviour would either fail after the fix or silently keep testing the wrong rule; D22 records why the narrower rule is correct.

deviations.what: Fixed a crash the narrowing introduced: PortalRolePermissionBackend.has_perm raised ValueError on a permission string with no app label (e.g. user.has_perm("change_project", project)), which tests/test_core/test_project/test_factories.py's guardian-backed fixtures use and which the prior wide implementation happened to answer False for instead of raising. Added a guard (`if "." not in perm: return False`) and a regression test before fixing it.
deviations.why: This is not named in the brief, but it is squarely inside fairdm/permissions.py - the exact function this story narrows - and it broke three previously-green tests the moment the narrowing landed. The brief's own bar is 'the whole suite is green'; leaving a self-inflicted crash unfixed to stay narrowly in scope would have left the story red.
